# Synthetic fixture decks

Development, tests, screenshots and demos use these decks, never client material (`docs/PRODUCT_BRIEF.md`, "Source material and how to use it").

**Provenance:** generated by `scripts/fixtures/build_fixtures.py` (python-pptx 1.0.2). Every company, person, place, number and image is invented. The "photo" is a generated pattern. No license restrictions apply. To regenerate:

```bash
python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -r scripts/fixtures/requirements.txt
.venv/bin/python scripts/fixtures/build_fixtures.py
```

| Deck | Slides | Size | Covers |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `northwind-capabilities.pptx` | 6 | 16:9 | Text, bullets, picture, native table, shapes; **slide 5 is hidden** and has speaker notes marked "never export" |
| `harbor-bank-proposal.pptx` | 4 | 16:9 | Native column chart, picture, speaker notes |
| `legacy-case-study-4x3.pptx` | 2 | 4:3 | Older slide size (mixed aspect ratios), picture |

## Not covered yet

The delivery plan's corpus (`docs/DELIVERY_PLAN.md`, "Evaluation corpus and limits") also asks for these. They're still to add, mostly when upload is built:

- different fonts and custom masters/layouts
- reviewer comments, SmartArt, video, linked media
- malformed, oversized, duplicate and password-protected files
- confidential variants with different permissions

Real client decks are only for an export-quality check the product owner approves (questionnaire item 5). They stay outside git.

## SharePoint-style library (search and tagging tests)

`sharepoint-library/` holds 18 synthetic proposal decks laid out the way Alina described M Moser's archive on Oct 8, so search, AI tagging and folder-path metadata can be tested before real decks arrive.

**Provenance:** generated by `scripts/fixtures/build_sharepoint_library.py` (python-pptx 1.0.2). Every client, person, place and number is invented. To regenerate:

```bash
.venv/bin/python scripts/fixtures/build_sharepoint_library.py
```

| Folder | Decks | Covers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Submittals/<year>/<client>/` | 12 | Years 2024 to 2026, IDD, Business Proposal and SME decks, 2 decks at 4:3, text, shapes, a native table and a native chart |
| `Best of the Best/<category>/` | 6 | Copies of 2 decks per category, as the pre-sorted set M Moser plans to share |

`answer_key.csv` has one row per slide: file, year, client, sector, category, slide number and the slide type planted in it (Cover, About us, About the client, Team, Approach, Case study, How we connect, Values, Timeline, Fees, Subject matter expertise, Next steps). Use it to score tagging and search.

Notes:

- The default ingest reads only the top level of `tests/fixtures/`, so this folder doesn't change the existing library, export checks or accessibility tests. Point `SLIDEVAULT_LIBRARY_DIR` at it once ingest reads subfolders.
- Decks under `Best of the Best/<category>/` have no year in their path, so year should come back unknown from folder metadata.
- The same deck appears in both folders on purpose, as a test case for duplicate grouping.

### Search test queries

`search_queries.csv` holds 22 test searches in three styles: `keyword` (words that appear on the slide), `natural` (how people ask, e.g. "team slide from the Halcyon project in 2024") and `meaning` (different words, e.g. "who we are" for About us). Each row says what a correct result looks like (client, year, category, slide type or title words), checked against `answer_key.csv`. `npm run score:search` reports how many find a correct slide in the top 10. Baseline with keyword search on Oct 11: 3 of 22 (keyword 3 of 3, natural 0 of 13, meaning 0 of 6). Swap in the business development team's real queries when they arrive.
